original_content.knowledge_point: Computing the Acceleration of a Particle at a Given Moment Given Its Position Vector
original_content.problem:
The position vector $r,$ in meters, of a particle $P$ relative to a fixed origin $O$ at time $t$ seconds is given by

$$
r=⟨4{t}^{3/2}+4{t}^{2}+5,\,{t}^{3}-4{t}^{2}+t⟩,\,t>0.
$$

Calculate the magnitude of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t=1.$
original_content.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we need to differentiate the velocity vector. So first, we need to compute the velocity vector, which we can do this by differentiating the position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4{t}^{3/2}+4{t}^{2}+5),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3}-4{t}^{2}+t)⟩ \\  & =⟨6{t}^{1/2}+8t,\,3{t}^{2}-8t+1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(6{t}^{1/2}+8t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{2}-8t+1)⟩ \\  & =⟨3{t}^{-1/2}+8,\,6t-8⟩\end{aligned}
$$

To find the acceleration at time $t=1,$ we substitute $t=1$ into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(1) & =⟨3(1)^{-1/2}+8,\,6(1)-8⟩ \\  & =⟨3+8,\,6-8⟩ \\  & =⟨11,\,-2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the magnitude of the acceleration, we compute $|a(1)|:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|a(1)| & =|⟨11,\,-2⟩| \\  & =\sqrt{{11}^{2}+(-2)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{125} \\  & =5\sqrt{5}\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$
